title: CaseForge counterfactual laboratory, collection 1
label: Internally pre-registered challenges, written by the author of the rules. Not an independent benchmark.
protocol: The rule set, engine version, base scenarios and a fingerprint of the reasoner and policy sources are recorded under `frozen`.

Every variant was built and passed through the ordinary scenario lint before registration. The lint uses the reasoner to decide solvability, so the author knew each variant to be solvable in principle (or solvable only by escalation, where stated).

Expectations and predictions were committed in the project's development history before any challenge other than `control` was run; `control` was used to develop the runner. That history is not part of the public repository, so the order cannot be verified from it.
No rule or policy is changed in response to a result. A challenge found defective after running is reported as such and amended only as a new revision, with the reason.

Revision for publication (2026-11-16), wording only: the question of `one_voice_two_doors` no longer cites an internal review identifier, `frozen` no longer names a commit of the unpublished development history, and the third item of this protocol says where the order of registration was recorded. No variant, edit, expectation, prediction, policy, rule or seed changed. The whole collection was then run again under the same frozen baseline; docs/LAB.md compares that run with the first.

categories.innocent_custodian: Somebody who lawfully had the means, and is innocent.
categories.surviving_lie: False testimony that no evidence available to the team can refute.
categories.mistaken_testimony: Honest testimony that is wrong, or right and discounted.
categories.route_variation: The same facts reachable only by a different path.
categories.provenance_conflict: Contradictory evidence of different kinds and origins.
categories.role_permutation: A different culprit, with the evidence rewritten to stay consistent.

curator_did_it.summary: The same building, people and sources, with the roles exchanged: the curator took the book on Friday. The two instruments that date the exchange now say Friday, the curator's own account becomes the false one and the night guard's the true one.

ops.why: who and when
culprit, account, and the records and facts that carry the case

fields.solution: Alan Fenwick exchanged the book. He drew the case key on Friday evening to prepare the loan, was alone in the Treasury from 18:09 to 19:42 with the alarm off, opened the case at 18:31 and left a facsimile in it. The sale he had proposed and the board had refused was his reason. The conservator's condition check on Thursday was what it claimed to be: she had the book out for twelve minutes and put it back. Fenwick's account, that the book was already a copy when he sat down beside it, is false.

ops.why: the logger must agree with the new truth: Thursday shows only the scheduled twelve-minute check, Friday the long unscheduled opening

fields.text: Microclimate logger, Treasury display case, 5 to 10 March. Thursday 6 March, 19:41 to 19:53: a twelve-minute excursion, matching the scheduled condition check. Friday 7 March, 18:31 to 19:38: the case stands open for sixty-seven minutes, with two changes of load on the cradle sensor. Nothing was scheduled. The book was exchanged on Friday evening.

ops.why: the photograph must agree with the new truth: the original was still there on Friday morning

fields.text: Comparison of the loan photograph taken on Friday 7 March at 10:15 with the 2019 digitisation: the book photographed on Friday morning is the original, with the old repair in the lower margin of folio 14. The facsimile has no such repair. The original was still in the case on Friday morning, after Thursday's condition check.

challenges.question: A door log puts Bob in the vault at night; a camera puts him in the cafe at the same time. One of the two instruments is wrong (the camera's clock, in fact). Records in a playable scenario must be true, so this conflict can only be posed to the reasoner directly.
challenges.prediction: 4 against 4: his presence is disputed, his opportunity contested, nobody is convicted. That is what a careful investigator should do with two instruments and no way to choose.

expectations.says: the conclusion does not depend on the order in which the items arrive
nobody is convicted while two records contradict each other
his presence in the vault is held as disputed, not believed and not rejected
his opportunity is contested, not an alibi

expectations.says: the conclusion does not depend on the order in which the items arrive
the innocent keyholder is not convicted
